output.summary: A shrub native to Southwest China, specifically Guizhou, Hubei and Sichuan, the China rose grows in hedges or thickets. Its wild form has five pink-to-red petals and red hips, while its purplish-brown branches may bear many curved spines or none.
output.edibilityNote: Young plant parts, flower buds and flowers are brewed or eaten; rosehip flesh is eaten raw or cooked, and ground seeds are added to foods.
